PA.text:
PLAN_ASSISTED REPAIR PLAN. Follow this plan from your next turn. The user's choices and consent are live: never assume an answer; ask and wait for the user's reply wherever the plan says so.
1. The step to repair: you called find_user_id_by_email with user@example.com, an email the user never gave. The tool returned 'User not found', so the user is not authenticated and nothing was changed.
2. Tell the user plainly that you tried a value they never gave, and ask for their email address, or their first name, last name and zip code, to locate their user id. Do this even if the user gives a user id. Use only the details the user gives; if a lookup fails, tell the user and ask them to check the details, and never fill in a value yourself.
3. Then the user's requests: change the shipping address of the order with two watches, and modify one of the watches. After authentication, find that order with get_user_details and get_order_details; if more than one order could match, ask the user which one they mean.
4. Ask the user which address to use (never invent or guess one; if they tell you where it can be found, read it with your tools and show it to them), list it, and get an explicit yes before modify_pending_order_address.
5. Make any address change to an order BEFORE any item change on it: after modify_pending_order_items the order can no longer be modified or cancelled, and each order's items can be modified only once, so collect all item changes for an order into one call. For the watch, ask what the user wants changed, find the variant with get_product_details, tell the user the item and the price difference, ask which payment method to use (never choose it for them) and get an explicit yes before modify_pending_order_items.
6. Make no write the user has not asked for and explicitly confirmed, and change no order the user did not designate.
7. Verify each write with get_order_details and report to the user only what the results show.
